\tau_o=\operatorname{arsinh}(31a/(64B)),\quad
\tau_i=\operatorname{arsinh}(29a/(64B)),\quad\Delta=\tau_o-\tau_i,\\
M_\phi=b+s(B+a),\quad C_a=\max\{1,512/a,2(512/a)^2\},
 \quad\epsilon_p=\epsilon/C_a,\\
D=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\Delta^{-1}
       \log\max\{e,24M_\phi/(\epsilon_p\Delta)\}\right\rceil\right\},
 \qquad N_\phi=4(D+1).
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-activation-degree}

With $x_i=B\cos(2\pi i/N_\phi)$, compute for each layer

$$
\begin{gathered}
c_{j,0}=N_\phi^{-1}\sum_i\phi^{(j)}(x_i),\qquad
c_{j,k}=2N_\phi^{-1}\sum_i\phi^{(j)}(x_i)\cos(2\pi ki/N_\phi) (k>0),\\
\psi^{(j)}(z)=\sum_{k=0}^Dc_{j,k}T_k(z/B).
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-activation-polynomial}

Finite value-call errors of magnitude at most
$\epsilon_p/[4(D+1)e^{D\tau_i}]$ are allowed in this formula only.
Initialized training features below still use exact original values.

:::: {#lem-compression-setup-source-routine}
### Certified numerical source polynomials

Let $C_g=\max_j\{H_j+1,B_j+1\}$ and choose

$$
\begin{split}
K=\max\bigg\{&8,
 \left\lceil2\log_2\max\{1,16TV/e_d\}\right\rceil,
 \left\lceil\log_2\max\{1,8V\widehat R_n/b_n\}\right\rceil,\\
&\left\lceil\log_2\max\{1,128V\widehat R_nC_{\rm src}n^{3/2}/\varepsilon_v\}\right\rceil,
 \left\lceil\log_2\max\{1,64\sqrt nC_g/\varepsilon_v\}\right\rceil\bigg\},\\
J&=\lceil2T/\widehat R_n\rceil
 =\lceil\max\{4T/r_t,16TL_n\}\rceil.
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-numerical-orders}

Use $J$ equal physical-time panels. Starting at the original initialization,
compute Taylor coefficients through degree $K$ for the polynomial-activation
field $\widetilde F$ by

$$
[u]_{k+1}=\frac1{k+1}[h^k]\widetilde F
                   \left(\sum_{i=0}^k[u]_ih^i\right),\qquad 0\le k<K,
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-jet-recursion}

and advance to each polynomial endpoint. The forward and backward source
jets through degree $K$, computed with the same coefficients and
$\psi^{(j)}$, approximate every base source $h^{(j)}$ or
$\delta^{(j)}$ in Euclidean norm by at most $\varepsilon_v/16$
at every real time in its numerical panel. Queries are all real unit
inputs for Harmonic and the declared input list for Taylor.
If $\log(1/\varepsilon_v)=O(\ell)$ at fixed parameters, then

$$
J=O(\ell^{3/2}),\qquad K=O(\ell),\qquad D=O(\ell^{3/2}).
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-numerical-scales}
::::

:::: {.proof}
First verify the activation approximation. The ellipse with boundary
$z=B(w+w^{-1})/2$, $|w|=e^{\tau_o}$ is inside the half-strip,
and $|\phi(z)|\le M_\phi$. The inner ellipse contains disks of
radius $a/512$ around all points at distance at most $a/512$ from
the moving-ball preactivation rectangle: the squared normalized real
and imaginary coordinates are at most
$(1/8)^2+(226/232)^2<1$.
Also $0<\Delta<1$ and $\Delta\ge a/(64B)$.

Shifting the Fourier contour of $\phi(B\cos u)$ bounds its
degree-$k$ Chebyshev coefficient by $2M_\phi e^{-k\tau_o}$.
On the inner ellipse $|T_k(z/B)|\le e^{k\tau_i}$, so the
tail after $D$ is at most
$4M_\phi\Delta^{-1}e^{-(D+1)\Delta}$.
The discrete coefficient at frequency $k$ sums the Fourier coefficients
at $k+qN_\phi$, $q\in\mathbb Z$. Summing these aliases for
$k\le D$ bounds their polynomial error by
$8M_\phi(D+1)e^{-2(D+1)\tau_o}
 \le8M_\phi\Delta^{-1}e^{-(D+1)\Delta}$.
The degree prescription makes their sum at most $\epsilon_p/2$.
The allowed value-call error adds at most $\epsilon_p/2$ by summing
$D+1$ coefficient errors of size at most twice that error.
Cauchy's formula on the verified disks proves simultaneous errors at
most $\epsilon$ in values and the first two derivatives.

At a fixed state in a moving ball, subtract the original and polynomial
forward passes. Feature RMS error is at most $U_j\epsilon$;
preactivation RMS error is at most $11U_{j-1}\epsilon$.
The constraint $11\sqrt nU_*\epsilon\le a/512$ keeps every
polynomial argument in the verified approximation domain.
For carriers of coordinate maximum $M$, backward subtraction gives
response RMS error $Q_j(M)\epsilon$: its propagated term costs
$11(s+1)Q_{j+1}$, direct gate approximation costs $K_j^{\rm act}$,
and the changed original gate costs $11t_2MU_{j-1}$.
The gradient-block and prediction differences are thus at most
$Q_\xi\epsilon$ and $Q_f\epsilon$. Splitting their product
in @eq-compression-setup-field gives
$\|\widetilde F-F\|\le C_F\epsilon\le\zeta_F$ throughout
the moving ball. The passive-source substitution error, including
initialized images, is at most $C_p\epsilon\le\tau/2$ in each
coordinate.

On its concentric ball of radius $b_n/2$, vector-valued Cauchy in
each unit parameter direction gives
$\|D(\widetilde F-F)\|_{\rm op}\le2\zeta_F/b_n\le L_n/2$.
In particular $\widetilde F$ is $2L_n$-Lipschitz there.
For a real anchor $u_0$ with $\|u_0-\theta(t)\|\le b_n/8$,
consider holomorphic errors on $|h|\le\widehat R_n$ and the map

$$
e(h)\longmapsto u_0-\theta(t)+
 \int_0^h[\widetilde F(\theta(t+z)+e(z))-F(\theta(t+z))]\,dz.
$$

On the supremum ball of radius $b_n/2$ its contraction factor is
at most $1/4$. Its image norm is at most
$b_n/8+\widehat R_n\zeta_F+b_n/8\le9b_n/32$.
Successive iterates converge uniformly; Cauchy's formula shows the limit
is holomorphic. The fixed point is the unique local solution $v$ of
the polynomial field, and has discrepancy at most $5b_n/24<b_n/4$
from the true complex reference and velocity at most $2V$.
Conjugation and uniqueness make it real on the real diameter.

Its degree-$K$ Taylor polynomial $u$ on a half-radius real panel
has parameter tail at most $2V\widehat R_n2^{-K}$ and derivative
tail at most $2V(2K+4)2^{-K}$. It stays in the smaller moving ball,
and its defect against the original field is at most
$2V(2K+5)2^{-K}+\zeta_F$. Since $2K+5\le4\,2^{K/2}$
for $K\ge8$, the numerical order gives total integrated defect
at most $e_d$. Lemma @lem-compression-setup-defect on each already
computed prefix gives

$$
\|u-\theta\|\le2e^{A_n}e_d
 \le\min\{b_n/8,\tau/(2C_{\rm src}n)\}.
$$

This verifies the hypothesis for the next restart, starting with exact
initialization. Finite induction constructs the entire path, without a
test of an unknown trajectory norm or rejected panels.

For a base source $g$, let $g^0,g^p$ denote original and polynomial
activation evaluation, and $g_K$ its source Taylor polynomial along
$v$. On the complex disk $\|g^p(v)\|_2\le\sqrt n C_g$:
the original RMS bounds are $H_j,B_j$ and the proved substitution
error is less than one. Thus
$\|g_K-g^p(v)\|_2\le\sqrt n C_g2^{-K}\le\varepsilon_v/64$.
Split the remaining error exactly as

$$
g_K-g^0(\theta)=[g_K-g^p(v)]+[g^p(v)-g^0(v)]
              +[g^0(v)-g^0(u)]+[g^0(u)-g^0(\theta)].
$$

The second and fourth terms have Euclidean norm at most
$\sqrt n\tau/2=\varepsilon_v/64$. For the third use the
real source bound and the parameter tail, giving
$2V\widehat R_nC_{\rm src}n^{3/2}2^{-K}\le\varepsilon_v/64$.
This proves the four-term error bound in the statement.

Finally $M_c,L_n,A_n=O(\sqrt\ell)$,
$b_n^{-1}=O(\sqrt{n\ell})$, $\widehat R_n^{-1}=O(\sqrt\ell)$,
$C_p=O(n)$ and $Z_*=O(\sqrt\ell)$ at fixed parameters.
Hence the logarithms of all inverse tolerances are $O(\ell)$,
$\Delta^{-1}=O(\sqrt\ell)$, and the explicit formulas give
@eq-compression-setup-numerical-scales. Recurrence
@eq-compression-setup-jet-recursion is causal and differentiates only
the finite polynomials $\psi^{(j)}$.
::::

### Two source spaces with the original retained sizes {#sec-compression-setup-source-spaces}

Let $\mathcal A_n$ be the comparison coefficient in
@eq-compression-selected-coefficients, and let $\mathcal D$ be the
explicit endpoint coefficient in the proof of
@lem-compression-selected-fitting. Use

$$
\eta=\min\{1,Y,S,Y/(2n\mathcal A_n)\},\qquad
\mathcal D e^{-8\ell}\le Y/(2n).
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-transfer-tolerance}

The second inequality is an eventual scalar gate. The comparison proof
gives $\log(1/\eta)\le2\ell$ eventually for each fixed positive
admissible problem. Once each source space meets the hypotheses of
@prp-compression-selected with this $\eta$, its all-time error is at
most $\mathcal A_n\eta+\mathcal D e^{-8\ell}\le Y/n$.
For Taylor set $C_{\rm sel}=\beta^{60L}$ as in
[the polynomial-width assembly](#sec-compression-polynomial-assembly). Its coefficient bounds show that
this $\eta$ is no smaller than the conservative tolerance used there,
and @eq-compression-polynomial-taylor-tail-gate implies the displayed
tail inequality. The precise degree gate used below is
@eq-compression-polynomial-taylor-count-gate itself, without enlarging
its exponent. There is no additional qualitative width threshold for Taylor.

#### Taylor from real source nodes {#sec-compression-setup-taylor}

Write $M=m+p$. Let $U_0\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}$ have orthonormal
columns spanning the declared normalized inputs, $k\le\min(d,M)$.
Replace them by $U_0^\top v_i$ and the first matrix by
$W_0^{(1)}U_0$. Their norms and Gram are unchanged. First-layer
updates lie in the same span, so the original and reduced dense paths
agree on every declared query. A Gaussian first row projected by $U_0$
is standard Gaussian in $\mathbb R^k$. This is the exact reduction
used in @prp-compression-panel; the retained map costs at most $Md$.

Use the deterministic capped finite-panel source domain from
@lem-compression-polynomial-source. Its constants
$\eta_*,U_{\rm fin},\mathcal K$ are the explicit source recurrences
in [the source coefficient definitions](#sec-compression-src-coefficients), @eq-compression-src-uv and
@eq-compression-src-k. In particular they do not involve observed
trajectory norms. Put

$$
\begin{gathered}
\nu=\lambda/4,\quad a_0=\min(a,1),\quad
b_{\rm cap}=\log(e+\ell),\quad B_{\rm cap}=1+(S^2/\eta_*)b_{\rm cap},\\
r_{\rm cap}=\min\left\{\frac{a_0}{64YSU_{\rm fin}\sqrt\ell},
 \frac1{\beta^{300L}(1+\lambda B_{\rm cap})\sqrt{b_{\rm cap}}}\right\},\\
h(t)=\frac{\log(1+2\mathcal K r_{\rm cap}e^{\nu t})}{2\mathcal K},
\qquad d_h=\lambda/(8\mathcal K).
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-capped-panels}

Starting at $t_0=0$, set
$r_b=h(t_b)/[2(1+d_h)]$ and
$t_{b+1}=\min\{T,t_b+r_b/2\}$. These are the disks and panels
certified by @lem-compression-polynomial-source. Since $h$ is
nondecreasing and $d_h\le1/8$, the certified disk radius at every
real center is at least $4h(0)/9>h(0)/4$. This verifies the
uniform numerical disk used earlier. If $J_s$ denotes the number
of source panels, then

$$
J_s\le1+\beta^{400L}\left[(Y/\lambda)^2\sqrt\ell
                  +\lambda^{-1}\log(e+\ell)\right].
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-taylor-panels}

For the count, $h'\le1/8$ makes each full panel contribute at least
$1/5$ to $\int dt/h(t)$. Split this integral where
$2\mathcal K r_{\rm cap}e^{\nu t}=1$, using $\log(1+x)\ge x/2$
before the split and logarithmic growth of slope at least $\nu/2$
afterward. This gives

$$
J_s\le1+\frac{40}{\lambda r_{\rm cap}}
 +\frac{80\mathcal K}{\lambda}\log(1+4\ell/\log2).
$$

The reciprocal minimum is bounded by

$$
\frac1{\lambda r_{\rm cap}}\le
 \frac{1024U_{\rm fin}}{a_0}(Y/\lambda)^2\sqrt\ell
 +\beta^{300L}\lambda^{-1}\sqrt{b_{\rm cap}}
 +\beta^{300L}B_{\rm cap}\sqrt{b_{\rm cap}}.
$$

Writing $x=\log\ell\ge0$, one has $b_{\rm cap}\le2+x$ and
$(2+x)^{3/2}e^{-x/2}\le4$. Thus $b_{\rm cap}^{3/2}\le4\sqrt\ell$.
Use $S^2=256(Y/\lambda)^2$, $\eta_*^{-1}\le\beta^{25L+4}$,
$U_{\rm fin}\le\beta^{26L}$ and $a_0^{-1}\le\beta$ to obtain
@eq-compression-setup-taylor-panels, with no confidence factor or
new logarithmic storage power. Also $2\mathcal K r_{\rm cap}\le1$,
so $h(0)\ge r_{\rm cap}/2$ and $h(0)^{-1}=O(\sqrt\ell)$
at fixed parameters. Therefore the numerical orders remain
@eq-compression-setup-numerical-scales. The cap need never be inactive.

Put $M_n=\beta^{6L}\sqrt n$ and

$$
K_s=\max\{8,\lceil2\log_2(64M_n/\eta)\rceil\},\quad
N_s=J_s(K_s+1),\quad
\varepsilon_v=\eta/[128(K_s+1)].
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-taylor-nodes}

On each panel $[t_b,t_{b+1}]$, use its $K_s+1$ transported
Chebyshev roots
$t_b+(t_{b+1}-t_b)[1+\cos((i+1/2)\pi/(K_s+1))]/2$.
Obtain base-source vectors from @lem-compression-setup-source-routine.
Use forward vectors on all $M$ inputs and backward vectors on the
$m$ training inputs. Insert their exact initialized images.
The nodal vectors themselves generate the space; interpolation coefficients
need not be retained or computed.

To verify accuracy, interpolation $I_{K_s}$ at those roots obeys
$\|I_{K_s}g\|_\infty\le(2K_s+1)\max_i|g_i|$ by discrete
cosine orthogonality and $|T_j|\le1$. The same inequality holds
in Euclidean norm. The degree-$K_s$ Taylor polynomial on a half-radius
panel has coordinate error at most $M_n2^{-K_s}$. As interpolation
reproduces this polynomial,

$$
\|g-I_{K_s}g\|_\infty
 \le(2K_s+3)M_n2^{-K_s}
 \le4M_n2^{-K_s/2}\le\eta/16.
$$

This applies separately to each exact source and its initialized image.
The approximate base node has Euclidean error at most $\varepsilon_v$;
an initialized image has at most $8\varepsilon_v$. Its interpolated
perturbation is therefore at most $16(K_s+1)\varepsilon_v=\eta/8$.
Both families have coordinate error below $\eta$, and
$I_{K_s}(W_0\widetilde g)=W_0I_{K_s}\widetilde g$ exactly.
The transpose identity has the same proof.

After adding the constant, exact initialized training features and images,
and first-layer columns, the rank $r$ and actual selected width $q$ obey

$$
r\le R=2m+k+1+2(M+m)N_s,\qquad q\le9r.
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-taylor-rank}

Apply @prp-compression-selected with its source-dimension argument equal
to $R$. We verify the numerical source degree at the stated polynomial
gate rather than identifying it with the initialized-jet degree.
Put
$B_0=32\beta^{6L}(1+C_{\rm sel})\lambda^{-3/2}(1+Y^{-1})$.
At $n\ge B_0^4$ and the source gate, one has $\ell\ge16$ and
$\log B_0\le(\log n)/4$. For the active comparison-tolerance branch,
using $1+\lambda^{-1/2}\le2\lambda^{-1/2}$ gives

$$
\log(64M_n/\eta)
\le\tfrac32\log n+\log B_0+\log8
                +\sqrt\ell+\log(1+\sqrt\ell)
\le\tfrac94\ell+\log8.
$$

For the branches $\eta=Y$ and $\eta=1$ the bound is smaller;
$S\ge16Y$ cannot give a smaller branch. Consequently
$K_s+1\le\max\{9,(9/(2\log2))\ell+8\}\le8\ell$
for $\ell\ge16$. Squaring
@eq-compression-setup-taylor-panels and retaining its $(Y/\lambda)^2$
factor gives precisely the parameter order in
@eq-compression-panel-size, including $(Y/\lambda)^4\ell^3$.
The map and declared data add $O(Md)$. Passive labels are never used.

#### Harmonic from positive coefficient quadrature {#sec-compression-setup-harmonic}

Use the current source radii $r_t$ in
@eq-compression-setup-source-input and
$r_q=1/[\beta^{3L}\sqrt{(d+3)\ell}]$, with
$M_n=\beta^{6L}\sqrt n$ and $\alpha=r_t/(4T)$.
Require the eventual scalar gates $\alpha,r_q\le1$.
For $d\ge2$, take exactly the mode set of
@lem-compression-harmonic-approximation:

$$
\begin{gathered}
b_d=2d-2,\quad D_d=2^{d+1}d^{d-2},\quad
P_T=18D_db_d!2^{b_d+1}/(\alpha r_q^{b_d+1}),\quad
H_*=2\log(16M_nP_T/\eta),\\
\Lambda=\{(k,j,b):\alpha k+r_qj\le H_*,\ 1\le b\le h_j\},\quad
h_j={j+d-1\choose d-1}-{j+d-3\choose d-1},\\
N=|\Lambda|,\quad p_t=\lfloor H_*/\alpha\rfloor,\quad
j_*=\lfloor H_*/r_q\rfloor,\quad
H_{\rm sph}=\sum_{j\le j_*}h_j,\quad\mathcal Y=\max_{j\le j_*}\sqrt{h_j}.
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-harmonic-modes}

Impossible binomials are zero. For a scalar source $g$, its coefficient
is

$$
c_{kjb}=\gamma_k\int_0^{2\pi}\!\int_{S^{d-1}}
g(T(1+\cos u)/2,v)\cos(ku)Y_{jb}(v)\,d\sigma(v)\frac{du}{2\pi},
\quad\gamma_0=1,\quad\gamma_k=2\ (k>0),
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-harmonic-coefficient}

where $Y_{jb}$ are real orthonormal harmonics for probability surface
measure. The proof of @lem-compression-harmonic-approximation bounds
the omitted-mode tail by $\eta/16$.

Here are finite quadrature orders and their construction. For $d\ge3$
use polar angles $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_{d-2}$ and azimuth
$\varphi$ in the usual recursive coordinates
$v=(\cos\theta_1,\sin\theta_1u)$; for $d=2$ use only
$v=(\cos\varphi,\sin\varphi)$. Define

$$
\begin{gathered}
I_0=\pi,\quad I_1=2,\quad I_b=(b-1)I_{b-2}/b,\quad
A_d=\prod_{b=1}^{d-2}\pi/I_b,\\
a_t=\alpha/2,\quad h_{\rm ang}=r_q/[2(d-1)],\quad
\sigma=\operatorname{arsinh}(2h_{\rm ang}/\pi),\\
\epsilon_c=\eta/(16N\mathcal Y),\quad
\delta_{\rm node}=\eta/(64NA_d\mathcal Y^2),\\
B_{\rm int}=2M_n\mathcal YA_d
 e^{a_tp_t+j_*(d-1)h_{\rm ang}}
                 (\cosh h_{\rm ang})^{(d-2)(d-1)/2},\\
N_t=\max\{1,\lceil a_t^{-1}\log(1+4dB_{\rm int}/\epsilon_c)\rceil\},\\
N_\varphi=\max\{1,\lceil h_{\rm ang}^{-1}\log(1+4dB_{\rm int}/\epsilon_c)\rceil\},\\
N_\theta=\max\{1,\lceil\sigma^{-1}
 \log[8dB_{\rm int}/(\epsilon_c(1-e^{-\sigma}))]\rceil\}\quad(d\ge3),\\
N_x=N_\varphi N_\theta^{d-2}\quad(d\ge3),\qquad N_x=N_\varphi\quad(d=2).
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-quadrature-orders}

Empty products equal one. Apply equal-weight periodic trapezoids with
$N_t,N_\varphi$ nodes to $u,\varphi$. For each polar coordinate,
transport to $\theta=\pi(1+x)/2$ the nodes and weights

$$
\omega_i=(2i+1)\pi/(2N_\theta),\quad x_i=\cos\omega_i,\quad
w_i=\frac1{N_\theta}\left[1-2\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor(N_\theta-1)/2\rfloor}
                    \frac{\cos(2k\omega_i)}{4k^2-1}\right].
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-fejer}

Multiply the spatial weights by
$\prod_{i=1}^{d-2}(\pi/I_{d-1-i})\sin^{d-1-i}\theta_i$.
The identity $I_b=\int_0^\pi\sin^b\theta\,d\theta$ follows by
integration by parts; the product is the normalized spherical Jacobian.

For completeness, the quadrature error follows directly from convergent
series. A periodic function bounded by $B$ on an analytic strip of
half-width $a$ has Fourier coefficients bounded by $Be^{-a|k|}$.
The trapezoid retains exactly the frequencies divisible by its order, so
its error is at most $2B/(e^{aN}-1)$.
Discrete cosine orthogonality at the polar roots gives the interpolant
$N_\theta^{-1}\sum_i g_i[1+2\sum_{k=1}^{N_\theta-1}
\cos(k\omega_i)T_k(x)]$. Its normalized integral is
@eq-compression-setup-fejer because the integral of an odd Chebyshev
mode is zero and that of mode $2k>0$ is $-1/(4k^2-1)$.
Thus this rule is exact through degree $N_\theta-1$. Its weights
are positive since $2\sum_{k=1}^q(4k^2-1)^{-1}=1-(2q+1)^{-1}<1$,
and sum to one. A Chebyshev tail on the ellipse of parameter
$e^\sigma$ is at most $2Be^{-N_\theta\sigma}/(1-e^{-\sigma})$.
The exact integral and positive rule each have norm one, so their
difference is at most twice this tail.

The domains needed for these bounds hold jointly. A complex plane
rotation of imaginary angle $y$ sends a point of the quadric whose
imaginary norm is $\sinh r$ to one with imaginary norm at most
$\sinh(r+|y|)$. This follows by writing its real and imaginary
parts, of norms $\cosh r,\sinh r$, and bounding the rotation's
two parts by $\cosh|y|,\sinh|y|$. Successive rotations with
all angle imaginary parts at most $h_{\rm ang}$ therefore stay
in the quadric tube of radius $r_q/2$. Each harmonic is separately
a trigonometric polynomial of degree at most $j_*$ in each angle.
The maximum-modulus argument for its Laurent polynomial gives bound
$\mathcal Ye^{j_*(d-1)h_{\rm ang}}$. The angular Jacobian has
bound $A_d(\cosh h_{\rm ang})^{(d-2)(d-1)/2}$.
The coefficient integrand is consequently bounded by $B_{\rm int}$.
The polar ellipse has imaginary angular height
$(\pi/2)\sinh\sigma=h_{\rm ang}$.

Telescoping the product of $d$ one-dimensional integral/rule operators
now bounds exact-value coefficient error by

$$
B_{\rm int}\left[\frac2{e^{a_tN_t}-1}
 +\frac2{e^{h_{\rm ang}N_\varphi}-1}
 +\frac{4(d-2)e^{-\sigma N_\theta}}{1-e^{-\sigma}}\right]
 \le\epsilon_c/2.
$$

Run @lem-compression-setup-source-routine with
$\varepsilon_v=\delta_{\rm node}$. Its base error is smaller
than $\delta_{\rm node}/8$ in Euclidean norm; an initialized image
therefore has coordinate error at most $\delta_{\rm node}$.
The spatial weights have total mass at most $A_d$, so the nodal
perturbation in any coefficient is at most
$2A_d\mathcal Y\delta_{\rm node}=\epsilon_c/2$.
Summing coefficient errors and the independent analytic tail gives
$\eta/16+N\mathcal Y\epsilon_c=\eta/8$.

Accumulate global coefficients only for the base sources and form
their initialized images afterward. Every coefficient is the same finite
scalar sum for each member of a pair, so
$\widetilde c^{\,W_0g}=W_0\widetilde c^{\,g}$ exactly.
Apply the preceding error proof separately to the analytic source and
its analytic image. This avoids converting coordinate errors through an
uncontrolled matrix norm. The source rank remains
$R=2m+d+1+4N$, and @prp-compression-selected applies.

For $d=1$, use the two points, $N_x=H_{\rm sph}=2$,
$H_1=\log(64M_n/(\alpha\eta))$, $N_1=1+\lfloor H_1/\alpha\rfloor$,
$p_t=N_1-1$, $N=2N_1$, and $R=2m+d+1+8N_1$.
Take $\epsilon_c=\eta/(16N_1)$,
$\delta_{\rm node}=\eta/(64N_1)$, $B_{\rm int}=2M_ne^{a_tp_t}$,
and $N_t=\max\{1,\lceil a_t^{-1}\log(1+4B_{\rm int}/\epsilon_c)\rceil\}$.
Only the time trapezoid is used. Its error allocation is identical;
the one-dimensional analytic tail is at most $\eta/8$ by
@lem-compression-harmonic-approximation, still leaving total error below
$\eta$.

The count proof of @prp-compression-harmonic applies to this identical
mode set and the same logarithmic tolerance. In particular its factor
$\alpha^{-1}=128\beta^{30L}(Y/\lambda)^2\sqrt{d+3}\ell^{3/2}$
is preserved before squaring the rank. This proves the complete retained
bound @eq-compression-harmonic-size, with its label and dimension factors.

### Exact implicit Gaussian execution {#sec-compression-setup-implicit}

The next finite-dimensional sampler is useful because the numerical
construction accesses an initialized hidden matrix only through its actions.
All its zero tests and normalizations are exact.

:::: {#lem-compression-setup-gaussian-sampler}
### Adaptive queries to both directions of a Gaussian matrix

For each of finitely many layers let the reference matrix have independent
$N(0,1/n)$ entries, independently across layers and of the client's
independent randomness. The client may choose the next layer, direction and
query vector measurably from that randomness and its complete past
transcript, and may stop within deterministic finite query budgets.
There is an online sampler whose entire transcript has exactly the dense
reference law. On an extension of its probability space, independent
Gaussian reference matrices can be completed so that every returned reply
is simultaneously the requested product with that one matrix.

For $Q$ requests to one layer, the sampler uses at most
$4nQ^2+6nQ+2$ scalar arithmetic operations, at most
$n\min\{Q,2n-1\}$ standard normal samples, and
$2n\min\{Q,2n\}+8n+5\min\{Q,2n\}+64$ real or address words.
These counts exclude the client's own work and retained arrays. The
completion matrices are proof objects, not arrays constructed by the algorithm.
::::

:::: {.proof}
For one layer keep matrices $V,Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ and
$U,R\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, initially empty, with

$$
V^\top V=I_p,\quad U^\top U=I_q,\quad U^\top Y=R^\top V.
$$

Their intended meanings are $Y=WV$ and $R=W^\top U$. For a
forward query $v$, compute
$a=V^\top v$, $v_\perp=v-Va$, $\alpha=\|v_\perp\|_2$.
If $\alpha=0$, return $Ya$. Otherwise put $e=v_\perp/\alpha$,
draw a fresh standard Gaussian vector $g$ if $q<n$, and set

$$
h=UR^\top e+n^{-1/2}[g-U(U^\top g)].
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-sampler-forward}

If $q=n$, omit the Gaussian term. Return $Ya+\alpha h$ and
append $(e,h)$ to $(V,Y)$. For a transpose query $u$, compute
$b=U^\top u$, $u_\perp=u-Ub$, $\alpha=\|u_\perp\|_2$.
If this is zero return $Rb$. Otherwise set $f=u_\perp/\alpha$ and

$$
h=VY^\top f+n^{-1/2}[g-V(V^\top g)],
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-sampler-transpose}

using a fresh standard Gaussian vector only when $p<n$.
Return $Rb+\alpha h$ and append $(f,h)$ to $(U,R)$.
Each layer has its own quadruple; all Gaussian vectors are independent.
No dense projector is formed in these operations.

Here is the conditional-law proof, including adaptation. For proof only
write $P=VV^\top$, $Q_0=UU^\top$ and
$A=YV^\top+UR^\top(I-P)$. Compatibility gives $AV=Y$,
$A^\top U=R$. The homogeneous solution space to these observations
is exactly $\{(I-Q_0)B(I-P):B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\}$,
and $A$ is Frobenius-orthogonal to it. The induction invariant is
the conditional kernel

$$
W=A+(I-Q_0)G(I-P),\qquad G_{ij}\ {\rm independent} N(0,1/n).
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-sampler-kernel}

At the initial empty state this is the dense Gaussian law. Given the
entire past, the next query is fixed. For a new forward direction $e$,
the action is $We=UR^\top e+(I-Q_0)Ge$, which has exactly
@eq-compression-setup-sampler-forward's law. Put $P'=P+ee^\top$.
The remaining matrix splits as

$$
(I-Q_0)G(I-P)=((I-Q_0)Ge)e^\top+(I-Q_0)G(I-P').
$$

The vector and remaining matrix are independent: their coordinate
cross-covariances are
$n^{-1}(I-Q_0)_{ia}[e^\top(I-P')]_b=0$.
Jointly Gaussian linear functions with zero cross-covariance are
independent even in singular cases, since their joint characteristic
function $\exp(-\|A^\top s+B^\top t\|^2/(2n))$ factors
when $AB^\top=0$. Thus observing the returned action changes only
the conditional mean by
$(h-UR^\top e)e^\top$ and replaces $P$ by $P'$.
Expanding the new stored-state formula for $A$ gives exactly this
new mean. Also $U^\top h=R^\top e$, preserving compatibility.

For a new transpose direction $f$, put $Q_0'=Q_0+ff^\top$.
The split is
$f((I-P)G^\top f)^\top+(I-Q_0')G(I-P)$, with zero
cross-covariance for the same reason. The new mean is
$A+f(h-VY^\top f)^\top$, exactly its new stored-state formula.
Dependent queries are already determined by the past and leave the kernel
unchanged; full opposite rank makes the innovation identically zero.

Conditional on the global transcript, kernels of different layers remain
a product. A query to one layer conditions only its factor; its choice
reveals nothing further because it is already measurable from the past.
Induction over the bounded number of requests proves equality of complete
transcript laws. A bounded stopping time is handled by partitioning into
its finitely many stopping events. At the stop, define completed matrices
by @eq-compression-setup-sampler-kernel with fresh independent $G$'s.
Their conditional kernels agree with the dense model; integration over
the identical transcript law proves the entire joint dense law, including
independence from client randomness. Their actions on the final $V,U$
are the stored $Y,R$, so every earlier reply is pathwise the correct
action of the single completed matrix.

A new forward query at current ranks $p,q$ costs at most
$6np+8nq+9n+1\le8n(p+q)+10n$ operations by direct dot-product
counts. A dependent query is cheaper, and the transpose count exchanges
the two ranks. Before request $j$, $p+q\le j-1$, giving
$4nQ^2+6nQ$ operations plus two for $1/\sqrt n$.
There are at most $2n-1$ drawing rank increments before one rank
reaches $n$; after that all new opposite directions are determined.
The four column lists use $2n(p+q)$ words. Eight length-$n$ scratch
vectors, five words per column for coefficients and addresses, and 64
scalar words give the displayed memory bound. Exact zero tests and rank
comparisons add at most two comparisons per request. No condition-number
or nonsingular query-Gram hypothesis is needed in this real-arithmetic
statement.
::::

#### Factored numerical anchors and output coupling {#sec-compression-setup-factored-execution}

Fix the numerical orders, scalar routines, generator ordering,
Gram--Schmidt signs, selector tie-breaking and other deterministic choices.
On numerical panel $b$, write $\Delta_b$ for its length and use
unscaled coefficients in $t-\tau_b$. For the polynomial-activation
training network let
$U_i^{(j)}=([r_a\delta_a^{(j)}]_i)_{a=1}^m$ and
$H_k^{(j)}=([h_a^{(j)}]_k)_{a=1}^m$, both $n$ by $m$ matrices.
Coefficient comparison in the actual gradient equations gives, for $s\ge1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
[W^{(1)}]_s&=-\frac2{ms}U_{s-1}^{(1)}(v_a)_{a=1}^m{}^\top,\\
[W^{(j)}]_s&=-\frac2{mns}\sum_{i+k=s-1}U_i^{(j)}H_k^{(j-1)\top},\\
[W^{(L+1)}]_s&=-\frac2{ms}\sum_a[r_ah_a^{(L)}]_{s-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-factored-jets}

Only lower orders are needed for an order-$s$ parameter coefficient.
The increment's action on a query series $X$ at order $s$ is

$$
-\frac2{mn}\sum_{i+k+c=s-1}
             \frac{U_i^{(j)}(H_k^{(j-1)\top}X_c)}{i+k+1}.
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-cached-action}

Cache all inner products $H_k^\top X_c$ before taking the outer
linear combinations. For a batch of $b'$ queries the work is
$O(mb'K^2(n+K))$ per layer: inner products and vector combinations
cost $O(nmb'K^2)$, scalar weighted sums $O(mb'K^3)$.
The transpose calculation exchanges the two factors.
This calculation is causal for training jets and applies to all passive
jets after the training coefficients are available.

The endpoint update groups into $mK$ outer products per hidden layer:

$$
W_{b+1}^{(j)}-W_b^{(j)}
=-\frac2{mn}\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}U_i^{(j)}V_i^{(j-1)\top},\qquad
V_i^{(j-1)}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1-i}
             \frac{\Delta_b^{i+k+1}}{i+k+1}H_k^{(j-1)}.
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-anchor-increment}

For the explicit execution, form each $V_i$ then add its outer
products to the dense anchor. For implicit execution append these pairs
to factors $A_b^{(j)},B_b^{(j)}\in\mathbb R^{n\times bmK}$,
including the scalar factor in $A_b$, so that

$$
W_b^{(j)}=W_0^{(j)}+A_b^{(j)}B_b^{(j)\top},\qquad
W_b^{(j)}X_c=\operatorname{Action}_j(X_c)
                  +A_b^{(j)}(B_b^{(j)\top}X_c).
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-implicit-anchor}

Transpose actions use the same factors exchanged. This is an exact
representation of the finite numerical anchor, not a rank assertion for
the continuous dense trajectory. The first matrix remains explicit;
its higher coefficient acts through the training input inner products in
@eq-compression-setup-factored-jets. It needs no array of $K$ dense
first-matrix coefficients. The readout is an ordinary vector.

The complete list of hidden initialized-matrix requests is:

1. $m$ forward actions per mixer for exact original initialized training
   features and their images. These use $\phi^{(j)}$, not $\psi^{(j)}$.
   Initial backward fields are zero.
2. Constant-anchor actions on each source/training coefficient through $K$
   on each numerical panel. The current-panel higher coefficients and
   previous-panel increments use the finite factors just displayed.
3. Initialized images of completed Harmonic coefficients or Taylor nodes.
4. $W_0^{(j)}U_{j-1}$ for the final source basis columns, after
   orthogonalization. Their number is at most the actual source rank $r$.
   Previously paired sources need not span all these image requests.

For Harmonic, all $N_x$ quadrature inputs require both directions;
training uses $m$ in both directions. For Taylor the $M$ forward
inputs already include training, and only its $m$ training inputs need
backward jets. Thus sufficient per-mixer query counts are

$$
Q_{\rm H}=m+2J(m+N_x)(K+1)+2N+r,\qquad
Q_{\rm T}=m+J(M+m)(K+1)+(M+m)N_s+r.
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-query-counts}

To invoke @lem-compression-setup-gaussian-sampler, replace random $r$
in the budget by the deterministic $\min(n,R)$. The cost may still
be bounded afterward using its actual value. No entry, norm, singular
value or other information about a hidden initialized matrix is accessed.

Under the sampler's completion coupling, run the explicit numerical
initializer with the completed matrices. Its exact initialized features
agree by layer induction. Assuming all earlier coefficients agree,
@eq-compression-setup-implicit-anchor and
@eq-compression-setup-cached-action give the same next matrix action.
All remaining operations use identical real operands, so coefficient
induction and then panel induction give the same sources and initialized
images. Their ordered generator lists agree, hence so do exact ranks,
bases, selector comparisons and selected weights. For source bases
$U_j^\top U_j/n=I$, selected row matrices $P_j=(U_j)_{I_j}$,
and source metrics $M_j$, item 4 gives the same core matrix
$U_j^\top W_0^{(j)}U_{j-1}/n$ and thus the same initialized mixer

$$
B_C^{(j)}(0)=P_j\frac{U_j^\top W_0^{(j)}U_{j-1}}n
                         P_{j-1}^\top M_{j-1}.
$$

The first-weight restriction, zero raw readout, initial deficit $c_C=y$,
exact initial training Gram, and corrected-readout caches likewise agree.
Thus the final arrays and their autonomous future agree pathwise, not only
in marginal law. The full source/fitting event retains its probability
with no extra failure budget. All sampler transcripts and trained factors
are discarded once the retained arrays have been formed.

### Complete operation and storage ledgers {#sec-compression-setup-costs}

All big-$O$ constants in the finite-order formulas below are numerical.
They hide no problem parameter, numerical order, scalar-evaluator cost or
confidence dependence. Assume $n\ge\max(m,d)$; the theorem is
eventual, and full-width exact retention is available otherwise when the
source budget is not smaller than $n$. Throughout, $R$ is the
generator count bound, $r$ the maximum actual rank, and $q$ the
maximum actual selected support size, so $r\le\min(n,R)$ and
$r\le q\le9r$. They are not the source-dimension symbol used in
@prp-compression-selected.

#### Scalar geometry, global coefficients, and selection {#sec-compression-setup-geometry-cost}

For Harmonic, assign each time node $t_a=T(1+\cos u_a)/2$ to
one numerical panel, retaining multiplicity if two time angles have the
same physical time. Let $I_b$ be those node indices. Form

$$
\mathcal B_{kc}^{(b)}=\frac{\gamma_k}{N_t}\sum_{a\in I_b}
 \cos(ku_a)((t_a-\tau_b)/\Delta_b)^c.
$$

If $[g]_c(v_s)$ is an unscaled local source coefficient, first multiply
it by $\Delta_b^c$ to obtain $G_{b,c}(v_s)$. Its global coefficient
is exactly

$$
\widetilde c_{kjb'}=
 \sum_b\sum_s\omega_sY_{jb'}(v_s)
                  \sum_{c=0}^K\mathcal B_{kc}^{(b)}G_{b,c}(v_s).
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-streamed-projection}

Process one panel's shared training jets, then its spatial queries,
then advance the anchor. Accumulate spatial coefficients first and
transform only the retained mode pairs. The scalar tables cost
$O((N_t+J)(p_t+1)(K+1))$ work, and projection costs
$O(LnJ(K+1)(N_xH_{\rm sph}+N))$ work with
$O(Ln(K+1)H_{\rm sph})$ extra vector words. Only $O(LnR)$
global coefficient words persist across panels. Local panels do not
create separate retained Harmonic source blocks.

We give the finite basis evaluation needed by these costs. On a circle
use $1,\sqrt2\cos(j\varphi),\sqrt2\sin(j\varphi)$ and angle-addition
recurrences. In dimension $d'\ge3$, writing
$v=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta\,u)$, recursively use

$$
(\sin\theta)^l C_{j-l}^{\,l+(d'-2)/2}(\cos\theta)
                       Y_{lb}(u),\qquad 0\le l\le j,
$$

with scalar normalization. To verify this basis, substitution into the
sphere Laplacian gives eigenvalue $-j(j+d'-2)$. Lower harmonics are
orthogonal, and for a fixed lower harmonic the remaining inner product
has weight $(1-z^2)^{l+(d'-3)/2}$. The Gegenbauer equation is
$(1-z^2)y''-(2\mu+1)zy'+s(s+2\mu)y=0$; multiply it by
$(1-z^2)^{\mu-1/2}$ and integrate by parts. The boundary term
vanishes because $\mu\ge1/2$, and unequal eigenvalues give
orthogonality. The harmonic
dimension decomposition in @lem-compression-harmonic-approximation
makes this orthogonal family complete. Its recurrence is

$$
(s+1)C_{s+1}^{\mu}(z)=2(s+\mu)zC_s^\mu(z)
 -(s+2\mu-1)C_{s-1}^\mu(z),\quad C_0^\mu=1,\quad C_1^\mu=2\mu z.
$$

It follows by differentiating the generating function
$(1-2zt+t^2)^{-\mu}$. If $N_{l,s}$ is the squared angular norm
for probability-sphere measure and $\mu=l+(d'-2)/2$, then

$$
N_{0,0}=1,\quad
\frac{N_{l+1,0}}{N_{l,0}}=\frac{2l+d'-1}{2l+d'},\qquad
\frac{N_{l,s+1}}{N_{l,s}}=
 \frac{(s+2\mu)(s+\mu)}{(s+1)(s+\mu+1)}.
$$

The first ratio is the integration-by-parts ratio for powers of sine.
For the second, express $zC_s^\mu$ using the three-term recurrence
and equate its inner products with $C_{s+1}^\mu$ by symmetry of
multiplication by $z$. Thus norms need only these recurrences and
inverse square roots, not a gamma-function oracle. There are
$O((j_*+1)^2)$ degree pairs per intermediate dimension; combining
with lower bases uses at most $O(H_{\rm sph})$ products per dimension.

For definiteness recompute spatial basis values on each numerical panel.
The following matched time and memory geometry bounds include quadrature
weight construction, node generation and the preceding basis recurrence:

$$
\mathcal G_{\rm time}=\begin{cases}
N_t+J,&d=1,\\
N_t+N_x+JN_x(j_*+1),&d=2,\\
N_\theta^2+dN_\theta+N_t+N_\varphi+d+d(j_*+1)^2
 +JdN_x[1+(j_*+1)^2+H_{\rm sph}],&d\ge3,
\end{cases}
$$

$$
\mathcal G_{\rm memory}=\begin{cases}
N_t+1,&d=1,\\
N_t+N_x+j_*+1,&d=2,\\
dN_\theta+N_t+N_\varphi+d[1+(j_*+1)^2+H_{\rm sph}],&d\ge3.
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-geometry-counts}

In @eq-compression-setup-fejer, cosine recurrences cost
$O(N_\theta^2)$ total; precomputed sine powers cost
$O(dN_\theta)$, so coordinates and Jacobian weights cost $O(d)$
per spatial node. These operations account for every term just displayed.

For either model, process at most $R$ source generators against at
most $r$ basis columns, costing $O(LnRr)$. The constructive
selector in @lem-compression-selection takes at most $9r$ steps
per layer. Each step forms shifted $r$ by $r$ inverses in
$O(r^3)$ and tests all $n$ rows using $O(nr^2)$ quadratic-form
work. Since $r\le n$, total selector work is $O(Lnr^3)$.
This term is retained in every ledger.

For the final metric, suppress layer indices and let $P$ be the
selected basis rows, $\mathsf D$ the positive diagonal selector
weights and $G=P^\top\mathsf DP$. Formula @eq-compression-metric
and direct multiplication give

$$
M=\mathsf D+\mathsf DP(G^{-2}-G^{-1})P^\top\mathsf D,\quad
M^{-1}=\mathsf D^{-1}+P(I-G^{-1})P^\top,\quad
P^\top M=G^{-1}P^\top\mathsf D.
$$

All inverses here are of the positive $r$ by $r$ Gram, whose
eigenvalues lie in $[1,4]$. Forming metric caches and composing the
initialized core mixers costs $O(L(qr^2+r^3+q^2r))=O(Lq^2r)$.
An explicit initialized basis image costs $O(n^2r)$ per mixer;
implicit execution instead pays its requests in $Q$ and then
$O(nr^2)$ to contract with the other basis. The initial training
Gram and its factorization cost $O(nm^2+m^3)$ and $O(m^2)$
words. Exact source isometry makes it the same initial Gram in the
selected model.

One scalar degree-$D$ activation polynomial composed with a degree-$K$
series costs $O(DK^2)$ and $O(DK)$ scratch: at time coefficient
$k$ each of the $O(D)$ Chebyshev recurrence products costs
$O(k+1)$, summed over $k\le K$. Preparing coefficients and
the derivative polynomial costs $O(LD^2)$ once. Both online
training compositions and offline source compositions use this algorithm.

#### Supplied dense initialization {#sec-compression-setup-explicit-costs}

For Harmonic put $P_d=(L-1)n^2+n(d+1)$. A sufficient complete
arithmetic envelope is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&P_d+LD^2+mP_d+nm^2+m^3+L+d+m+1\\
&+JP_d(m+N_x)K+JLm(m+N_x)K^2(n+K)
 +JLn(m+N_x)DK^2\\
&+(N_t+J)(p_t+1)K+LnJK(N_xH_{\rm sph}+N)+Ln^2N\\
&+LnRr+Lnr^3+Ln^2r+Lq^2r
 +\mathcal G_{\rm time}+N_t\log(2+N_t)\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-explicit-harmonic-work}

Its sufficient peak real-coordinate count is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&P_d+LmnDK+Lm^2K^2+LnR+Lq^2+LnKH_{\rm sph}+LD\\
&+(p_t+1)K+N_t+J+m(d+1)+m^2+L+d
 +\mathcal G_{\rm memory}\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-explicit-harmonic-memory}

The constant-anchor actions cost $P_d(m+N_x)K$ per panel.
Cached higher-coefficient actions give the next term. Forming each
grouped endpoint factor in @eq-compression-setup-anchor-increment costs
$O(nmK^2)$, and adding its $mK$ outer products costs
$O(n^2mK)$ per layer and panel, absorbed in the same ledger.
The $Ln^2N$ and $Ln^2r$ terms separately pay initialized
source images and final basis images. The moment table, projection and
selection terms were proved above. A single numerical anchor, original
initialized arrays, current-panel jets and global coefficients are live;
no $JP_d$ trajectory or $KP_d$ dense jet array is stored.

For Taylor let $k$ be its reduced input dimension and
$P_k=(L-1)n^2+n(k+1)$. Its sufficient complete work is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&P_d+dM^2+ndk+LD^2+mP_k+nm^2+m^3+L+k+m+1\\
&+J\{P_k(M+m)K+Lm(M+m)K^2(n+K)+Ln(M+m)DK^2\}\\
&+LnMKN_s+Ln^2R+LnRr+Lnr^3+Lq^2r
 +N_s\log(2+N_s)+J_s+N_s\big),
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-explicit-taylor-work}

with sufficient peak memory

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&P_d+LnmDK+LnMK+LmMK^2+LnR+Lq^2+LD\\
&+N_s+J+J_s+Md+dk+m^2+L+k+m+1\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-explicit-taylor-memory}

The input reduction costs $O(dM^2)$ and the supplied first-matrix
projection $O(ndk)$. Evaluating source jets at the $N_s$ nodes
costs $O(Ln(M+m)KN_s)$, absorbed by the displayed $M$ term
since $m\le M$. Images and final basis actions are bounded by
$O(Ln^2R)$ together. Sort and merge the source nodes with the
numerical panels before the single continuation pass. Source nodes and
numerical panels are distinct partitions.

#### Fresh implicit Gaussian initialization {#sec-compression-setup-implicit-costs}

For Harmonic use $Q=Q_{\rm H}$ from
@eq-compression-setup-query-counts. A complete arithmetic envelope is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&nd(1+m)+m^2d+nm^2+m^3+L+d+m+1+L(D+1)^2\\
&+(L-1)nQ^2+(L-1)nm(m+N_x)J(J-1)K(K+1)\\
&+J[nd(m+N_x)+dmN_x]
 +JLm(m+N_x)(K+1)^2(n+K+1)\\
&+JLn(m+N_x)(D+1)(K+1)^2\\
&+(N_t+J)(p_t+1)(K+1)+LnJ(K+1)(N_xH_{\rm sph}+N)\\
&+LnRr+Lnr^3+(L-1)nr^2+L(qr^2+r^3+q^2r)+qd\\
&+\mathcal G_{\rm time}+N_t\log(2+N_t)\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-implicit-harmonic-work}

Its matched peak-memory envelope is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&nd+(L-1)n[Q+JmK]+Lmn(D+1)(K+1)+Lm^2(K+1)^2\\
&+LnR+Ln(K+1)H_{\rm sph}+Lq^2+q(d+Lm+1)+m^2+m(d+1)\\
&+L(D+1)+(p_t+1)(K+1)+N_t+J+L+d+m+1
 +\mathcal G_{\rm memory}\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-implicit-harmonic-memory}

The sampler pays $O((L-1)nQ^2)$ work and $O((L-1)nQ)$ memory.
At panel $b$ an accumulated trained factor has $bmK$ columns;
its action costs $O(nbmK)$ per coefficient vector. Summing the
$2(m+N_x)(K+1)$ possible vectors per panel gives the second term,
using $\sum_{b<J}b=J(J-1)/2$. Its factors occupy
$O((L-1)nJmK)$ words. Their grouped formation costs
$O(JLnmK^2)$, covered by the current-panel contraction term.
The explicit first matrix, input pairings, coefficient projection and
selector account for the remaining terms already proved above.

For Taylor, sample only the $n$ by $k$ reduced first matrix, and
use $Q=Q_{\rm T}$. It has the same law as $W_0^{(1)}U_0$;
the independent Gaussian component on the orthogonal input complement
may be completed in the proof. No request concerns that component.
A sufficient complete arithmetic bound is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&dM^2+nk(1+m)+km^2+nm^2+m^3+L+k+m+1+L(D+1)^2\\
&+(L-1)nQ^2+(L-1)nm(M+m)J(J-1)K(K+1)\\
&+J[nk(M+m)+kmM]
 +JLm(M+m)(K+1)^2(n+K+1)\\
&+JLn(M+m)(D+1)(K+1)^2+Ln(M+m)(K+1)N_s\\
&+LnRr+Lnr^3+(L-1)nr^2+L(qr^2+r^3+q^2r)+qk\\
&+N_s\log(2+N_s)+N_s+J+J_s\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-implicit-taylor-work}

Its sufficient peak real-coordinate count is

$$
\begin{split}
O\big(&Md+dk+nk+(L-1)n[Q+JmK]+Lmn(D+1)(K+1)\\
&+LnM(K+1)+LmM(K+1)^2+LnR+Lq^2+q(k+Lm+1)\\
&+m^2+Mk+L(D+1)+N_s+J+J_s+L+k+m+1\big).
\end{split}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-implicit-taylor-memory}

The factor-history term is charged exactly as for Harmonic, now with
$M$ forward and $m$ backward coefficient vectors per order.
All Taylor initialized node images and final basis images are included
in $Q$. The ledger includes node evaluation, source orthogonalization,
the $nr^3$ selector and the final Gram and metric solves.
Thus a small source rank has not been used to omit either reference
matrix queries or trained-factor multiplication.

#### Primitive costs and fixed-parameter bounds {#sec-compression-setup-specialization}

In each model there are $4L(D+1)+Lnm$ original real activation-value
calls, plus at most $L$ if the values at zero used in an envelope are
not supplied. Only the first $4L(D+1)$ calls may use the finite
tolerance in @eq-compression-setup-activation-polynomial.
There are no original derivative calls during setup. The retained runtime
uses original activation and first-derivative evaluations as before.

Supplied dense initialization needs no Gaussian draws. Fresh explicit
initialization, if desired, adds $nd+(L-1)n^2$ draws. The implicit
Harmonic draw count is at most $nd+(L-1)nQ_{\rm H}$; the implicit
Taylor count is at most $nk+(L-1)nQ_{\rm T}$. No readout draw is
needed. The unobserved completion draws are not algorithmic operations.
For Harmonic the additional elementary-function call count is at most

$$
O(L+d+m+1+L(D+1)+N_t+A_{\rm ang}+(L-1)Q+Lr),\quad
A_{\rm ang}=\begin{cases}
0,&d=1,\\N_x,&d=2,\\
N_\theta+N_\varphi+d(j_*+1)^2,&d\ge3.
\end{cases}
$$

For Taylor replace the time/angular terms by $N_s+J_s$ and add
$O(M)$ input-basis square roots. For explicit execution omit the
sampler's $Q$ term. These counts include scalar certificates, ellipse
orders, geometry tables, query normalizations and orthogonalization.
Rounding and mode enumeration require at most the displayed finite table
sizes. If scalar calls have nonconstant cost, add the sum of their actual
work and the largest simultaneously used evaluator scratch. The formulas
do not assume that analyticity computes its own envelopes, population gap
or evaluator.

For separately fixed admissible parameters,
@eq-compression-setup-numerical-scales and the source formulas give

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
&\text{Harmonic}&\text{Taylor}\\ \hline
J,D& O(\ell^{3/2})&O(\ell^{3/2})\\
K&O(\ell)&O(\ell)\\
\text{source sizes}&N_t,p_t+1=O(\ell^{5/2}),\quad
 N_x,H_{\rm sph}=O(\ell^{3(d-1)/2})&
 J_s=O(\ell^{1/2}),\quad K_s+1=O(\ell)\\
R,r,q&O(\ell^{3d/2+1})&O(\ell^{3/2})\\
Q&O(\ell^{3d/2+1})&O(\ell^{5/2}).
\end{array}
$$ {#eq-compression-setup-all-orders}

The two-point convention gives the same Harmonic exponents at $d=1$.
For the supplied dense variants the full ledgers respectively imply

$$
O(n^2\ell^{3d/2+1}+n\ell^{9d/2+3}+\operatorname{polylog}(n)),\qquad
O(n^2\ell^{5/2}+n\ell^5+\operatorname{polylog}(n)).
$$

At fixed parameters their second and third terms are eventually smaller
than their first, and their memory ledgers are $O(n^2)$.
For implicit Harmonic the sampler term is $O(n\ell^{3d+2})$;
trained-factor and activation work are $O(n\ell^{3d/2+7/2})$,
and projection exponents are at most $3d-1/2$ and $3d/2+7/2$.
The selector is $O(nr^3)=O(n\ell^{9d/2+3})$, dominating
every displayed width-proportional term for $d\ge1$. The remaining
terms are fixed powers of $\ell$. Its transcript, source coefficients
and other buffers fit $O(n\ell^{3d/2+1})$ memory.

For implicit Taylor the sampler term, accumulated trained-factor work,
and activation composition are each $O(n\ell^5)$:

$$
nQ_{\rm T}^2=O(n\ell^5),\qquad
nm(M+m)J^2K^2=O(n\ell^5),\qquad
Jn(M+m)DK^2=O(n\ell^5).
$$

The selector costs $O(n\ell^{9/2})$, and the other terms fit the
same work bound. Transcript, trained-factor and online activation storage
are $O(n\ell^{5/2})$; all other buffers fit this bound. These
substitutions prove all four rows of
@prp-compression-efficient-setup, including source construction, original
initialized additions, selection and final assembly.

At completion the dense anchors, source generators, bases, panel schedules,
activation polynomials, Gaussian transcripts and trained factors are
discarded. The retained inventories and nonlinear optimizer are exactly
those of the source-to-runtime theorem. Approximate generator construction
does not require preservation of an accidental rank deficiency: the
selector uses the span actually computed and the guaranteed generator
bound $R$. Exact initialized additions preserve the initial Gram and
pairing hypotheses. Their replacement by finite-precision values would
require an additional perturbation theorem, as would finite-precision
rank decisions, barrier comparisons and infinite-time runtime evolution.
The bounds here count real coordinates and operations, not bits.

The setup covers $T=32\ell/\lambda$ in physical time. Its small
number of numerical panels is not a claim about a short physical training
prefix. Ordinary dense Euler at physical step $h$ has work
$\Theta(mP_dT/h)$ before source assembly. At fixed parameters the
explicit Taylor and Harmonic setup/Euler ratios are bounded by
$O(h\ell^{3/2})$ and $O(h\ell^{3d/2})$, respectively. This
comparison specifies an Euler step; it neither proves that such a step
is necessary nor compares favorably against every high-order dense solver.

## Nonlinear feature learning preserved by compression {#sec-compression-nonlinear-learning}

A moving kernel alone does not distinguish nonlinear learning from a deep
linear network. We therefore separate nonaffinity of the predictor, departure
from frozen-feature training, and motion of the dense hidden features.
The frozen-kernel comparator belongs to the coupled dense reference, not to
the compressed model. Because $W^{(L+1)}(0)=0$, its initial tangent features
are precisely its initial last-layer features. Define its predictor by

$$
\partial_t f_{\mathrm{NTK},n}(t,x)
 =\frac{2}{mn}\sum_{a=1}^m
 h^{(L)}(0,x)^\top h^{(L)}(0,x_a)
 [y_a-f_{\mathrm{NTK},n}(t,x_a)],\qquad
 f_{\mathrm{NTK},n}(0,x)=0.
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-frozen}

This is exactly readout-only gradient flow with all hidden features fixed.

::: {#thm-compression-nonlinear-learning}
### Nonlinear feature learning preserved by compression

Under @thm-compression-headline's assumptions, suppose additionally that
every activation is nonaffine and $|x_a^\top x_b|<d$ for $a\ne b$.
For Taylor, augment $\mathcal X$ by at most four deterministic passive
witness inputs, declared before initialization without their labels.
There are $c_*,t_*>0$, depending on the fixed problem but not on width,
such that for every fixed $0<t\le t_*$, each compressed predictor satisfies,
with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\inf_{a\in\mathbb R^d,\,b\in\mathbb R}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
 |f_{\rm model}(t,x)-a^\top x-b|&\ge c_*t,\\
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
 |f_{\rm model}(t,x)-f_{\mathrm{NTK},n}(t,x)|&\ge c_*t^3.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-prediction-gaps}

The storage orders and approximation conclusions are unchanged; Taylor's
bound uses the augmented panel count, at most $p+4$ instead of $p$.
In the dense reference, every hidden layer satisfies

$$
\left({\frac1n\sum_{a=1}^m
 \|h^{(\ell)}(t,x_a)-h^{(\ell)}(0,x_a)\|_2^2}\right)^{1/2}
 \ge c_*t^2\qquad(1\le\ell\le L)
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-layer-motion}

with the same probability convention. The nonlinear part of the dense
first-layer feature increment has mean-square size at least $c_*t^4$,
as specified in @eq-compression-fl-nonlinear-increment.
:::

The first gap excludes every deep linear predictor, including biases and
time-dependent weights. The second excludes the dense reference's frozen
initial kernel, not all conceivable kernel methods. The internal conclusions
further rule out a frozen nonlinear feature component accompanied only by an
affine feature change. They do not identify compressed coordinates with dense
neurons. The additional hypotheses are local to this theorem and its proof;
the broader compression theorem does not require them.

The mechanism has three time scales. The initially zero readout grows at
order $t$; hidden features move at order $t^2$; the output departs from
frozen-feature training at order $t^3$. The leading departure in the label
direction is a sum of squared hidden-layer accelerations, so layers cannot
cancel one another's contribution. Separately, the initial feature kernel
has nonlinear input components that no nonzero label vector can cancel
completely. Both signals survive a vanishing absolute compression error.

These are early-time certificates, not endpoint or test-risk comparisons.
Time is fixed before taking the width limit: no compressed-model lower bound
uniform over arbitrary sequences $t_n\downarrow0$ is asserted. The new
constants may depend on the entire fixed problem, unlike the chapter's
activation-and-depth-only constant $C$.

### Initial geometry {#sec-compression-fl-initial-geometry}

The proof uses @lem-compression-fit and the absolute approximation bounds
already proved for the three constructions. All auxiliary notation below
is local to the supporting argument; constants in remainder estimates may
depend on the fixed problem, but not on width.

::: {#lem-compression-fl-input}
### Nonlinear initial velocity

Every $Q^{(\ell)}$, $\ell\ge1$, is positive definite. The limiting initial
prediction velocity is nonaffine on the sphere, witnessed by an
affine-annihilating combination of four deterministic inputs chosen before
initialization.
:::

[]{#proof-compression-fl-input}

::: {.proof}

Write $v=x/\sqrt d$. Gaussian covariance recursion gives
$Q^{(\ell)}_{ab}=F_\ell(v_a^\top v_b)$, $F_0(s)=s$, with

$$
F_\ell(s)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_{\ell,k}s^k,\qquad
c_{\ell,k}\ge0,\qquad \sum_kc_{\ell,k}<\infty,
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-positive-series}

and unbounded positive coefficient support. To see this directly, expand
$\phi^{(\ell)}(\sqrt q G)$ in orthonormal Gaussian Hermite polynomials,
with coefficients $\alpha_k$. Its covariance at correlation $r$ is
$\sum_k\alpha_k^2r^k$. The identity follows by comparing coefficients in
$\mathbb E[e^{zG-z^2/2}e^{wG'-w^2/2}]=e^{rzw}$.
Completeness follows because a function orthogonal to all polynomials has
entire transform $\mathbb E[h(G)e^{zG}]$ identically zero, hence zero Fourier
transform. Linear growth gives Gaussian $L^2$ integrability. Finite Hermite
support would make the activation a polynomial, hence affine by its bounded
derivative. Composing these covariance series with
$F_{\ell-1}(s)/F_{\ell-1}(1)$ proves @eq-compression-fl-positive-series:
Tonelli at $s=1$ gives summability, and a positive inner coefficient of
degree $j\ge1$ and outer degree $k$ produces degree $jk$. The recursion
starts with $F_0(s)=s$ and positive variance at every layer. Nonzero means
are allowed, and convergence is uniform and absolute on $[-1,1]$.
The tensor Grams $[(v_a^\top v_b)^k]$ are positive semidefinite and converge
to $I_m$ by the nonparallel-input hypothesis. Thus every $Q^{(\ell)}\succ0$.

Let $P$ project onto affine functions in spherical $L^2$ with normalized
surface measure $\sigma$:
$Ph(v)=\int h\,d\sigma+d\,v^\top\int uh(u)\,d\sigma(u)$.
Projecting the tensor feature in both variables gives the positive kernel

$$
R_k(v,u)=(v^\top u)^k-a_k-b_kv^\top u,\qquad
a_k=\int(z^\top u)^k\,d\sigma(z),\qquad
b_k=d\int(z^\top u)^{k+1}\,d\sigma(z).
$$

Here $a_k,b_k\to0$ by dominated convergence: the local input hypothesis
and $m\ge2$ imply $d\ge2$. Hence $[R_k(v_a,v_b)]\to I_m$.
The limiting velocity $g(v)=(2/m)\sum_a y_aF_L(v^\top v_a)$ cannot be affine,
since otherwise

$$
0=\sum_a y_a[(I-P)g](v_a)
 =\frac2m\sum_kc_{L,k}\,y^\top[R_k(v_a,v_b)]y>0.
$$

Every term is nonnegative and some large-degree term is positive. Uniform
convergence justifies projection and summation.

Some great circle witnesses this nonaffinity. Otherwise the antipodal
average of $g$ is constant, and the odd remainder extends homogeneously
to a function linear on every plane, hence globally linear. On such a
circle, interpolate three distinct points by an affine function and take
a fourth where it fails. Sign and normalize their affine dependence to obtain
unit vectors $u_i$ and coefficients satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^4|c_i|=1,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^4c_i=0,\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^4c_i u_i=0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^4c_i g(u_i)>0.
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-witnesses}

These inputs depend on the fixed problem only. The finite-query Gram
argument in @lem-compression-fit applies to this augmented list. Together
with
$\dot f_n(0,x)=(2/(mn))\sum_a y_a h^{(L)}(0,x_a)^\top h^{(L)}(0,x)$,
it gives convergence of the four initial velocities.
:::

::: {#lem-compression-fl-initial-fields}
### Initial backward fields and hidden forces

The initialized forward fields and first backward derivatives, including
the vectors before derivative gates, have deterministic joint empirical
row-law limits with second moments. This includes the full first-layer
weight and acceleration rows. Every hidden block's squared initial
acceleration in inverse-mobility norm converges to a positive constant.
:::

[]{#proof-compression-fl-initial-fields}

::: {.proof}

All unmarked fields in this proof are at zero. Put $k=2/m$ and define
the pre-gated vectors $P$ and their gated versions $B$ by

$$
P_a^{(L)}=\sum_b y_bh_b^{(L)},\qquad
B_a^{(\ell)}=(\phi^{(\ell)})'(z_a^{(\ell)})\odot P_a^{(\ell)},\qquad
P_a^{(\ell-1)}=(W^{(\ell)})^T B_a^{(\ell)}\quad(2\le\ell\le L).
$$

Thus $\dot\delta_a^{(\ell)}(0)=kB_a^{(\ell)}$. Since hidden velocities
initially vanish, differentiation of @eq-compression-flow gives

$$
\ddot W^{(1)}(0)=k^2\sum_a y_aB_a^{(1)}v_a^T,\qquad
\ddot W^{(\ell)}(0)=\frac{k^2}{n}\sum_a y_aB_a^{(\ell)}(h_a^{(\ell-1)})^T
\quad(2\le\ell\le L).
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-forces}

Only one forward pass and one backward pass are needed for their joint
limits. For a hidden Gaussian matrix $W$, after revealing $WH=Z$, its
conditional law on the full-column-rank event is
$Z(H^T H)^{-1}H^T+\widetilde W(I-\Pi_H)$, where
$\Pi_H=H(H^T H)^{-1}H^T$ and $\widetilde W$ is fresh with entries
$\mathcal N(0,1/n)$. This is orthogonal Gaussian conditioning on a linear
constraint. For a reverse query $U$ known from the preceding answers,

$$
\begin{aligned}
W^T U&\overset{\mathrm d}=H Q_n^{-1}C_n+(I-\Pi_H)\Xi D_n^{1/2},\\
Q_n&=H^T H/n,\qquad C_n=Z^T U/n,\qquad D_n=U^T U/n,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-conditioning}

where $\Xi$ has independent standard Gaussian rows. Conditioned on the
revealed data, the removed projection has expected squared Frobenius norm
divided by $n$ equal to
$\operatorname{rank}(H)\operatorname{tr}(D_n)/n$.
The row-law induction below makes $D_n$ tight, so conditional Markov's
inequality shows that this term vanishes in probability.

Adaptive queries do not create an unobserved matrix dependence. In the
forward pass, each new query is fixed by the previous answers. Conditioning
on its Gaussian action leaves independent residuals in the other matrices.
In the descending reverse pass, the query for a given matrix is determined
by the forward transcript and the reverse answers of higher matrices, not
by that matrix's unrevealed residual. No matrix is queried again after its
reverse answer. Thus @eq-compression-fl-conditioning applies at each step.

The induction uses empirical $\mathcal W_2$ convergence in probability on
the finite-dimensional space of row coordinates, with its Euclidean metric.
Appending independent Gaussian rows preserves a deterministic such limit:
conditional variances of bounded test averages are $O(1/n)$, and appended
second moments obey the law of large numbers. Continuous coordinate maps
of at most linear growth preserve this convergence by an $L^2$ coupling
and uniform integrability; these include $\phi(z)$ and $\phi'(z)u$.
Same-layer products consequently converge. Inverse Grams and covariance
square roots converge when their limiting Grams are, respectively,
positive definite and positive semidefinite. A row array with vanishing
mean squared norm does not change the limit, which disposes of the projected
term in @eq-compression-fl-conditioning.

Starting with the full independent first-layer rows, these rules prove the
forward and then backward limits, including pre-gated fields. Every forward
Gram inverted here is $Q^{(\ell)}$ with $\ell\ge1$, positive definite by
@lem-compression-fl-input, so the full-rank events have probability tending
to one; $Q^{(0)}$ is never inverted. The first-row acceleration is a linear
combination of the $B$ fields, so its joint limit is included.

Let $D^{(\ell)}$ be the limiting Gram of $B^{(\ell)}$.
At the top it is positive definite: a null vector $c$ would imply

$$
\left(\sum_b y_b\phi^{(L)}(z_b)\right)
\left(\sum_a c_a(\phi^{(L)})'(z_a)\right)=0
\qquad(z\in\mathbb R^m).
$$

Indeed $L\ge2$ gives full Gaussian support. The first factor is not
identically zero since $y^T Q^{(L)}y>0$; analyticity forces the second
to vanish everywhere. Varying each coordinate and using the nonconstant
derivative gives $c=0$. Downward, the fresh reverse innovation is independent
of the lower-layer fields, with covariance $D^{(\ell+1)}$, so

$$
c^T D^{(\ell)}c\ge\lambda_{\min}(D^{(\ell+1)})
 \sum_a c_a^2\mathbb E[((\phi^{(\ell)})'(Z_a^{(\ell)}))^2]>0
\qquad(c\ne0).
$$

Each Gaussian marginal is nondegenerate; a nonzero analytic derivative
has a zero set of measure zero. Expanding @eq-compression-fl-forces, the
layer-$\ell$ squared acceleration in inverse-mobility norm has limit
$k^4y^T(Q^{(\ell-1)}\circ D^{(\ell)})y>0$, where $\circ$ is entrywise
multiplication. For $Q\succeq0$ and $D\succ0$,
$Q\circ D\succeq\lambda_{\min}(D)\operatorname{diag}(Q)$: decompose $Q$
into rank-one terms and apply the lower bound for $D$ to each term.
Every relevant $Q$ has positive diagonal. This also covers singular input
Grams. The inverse-mobility squares here are
$\|\ddot W^{(1)}(0)\|_F^2/n$ and $\|\ddot W^{(\ell)}(0)\|_F^2$ for $\ell\ge2$.
:::

### Actual motion and the cubic departure {#sec-compression-fl-actual-motion}

::: {#lem-compression-fl-motion}
### Adjoint test of the actual motion

Every hidden layer satisfies @eq-compression-fl-layer-motion. On the training
set, regarding predictions as vectors in $\mathbb R^m$,

$$
y^T(f_n(t)-f_{\mathrm{NTK},n}(t))
=\frac m3 t^3\left[\frac{\|\ddot W^{(1)}(0)\|_F^2}{n}
 +\sum_{\ell=2}^L\|\ddot W^{(\ell)}(0)\|_F^2\right]+o_*(t^3).
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-cubic}

In this argument, $R_n(t)=o_*(t^j)$ means: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there
is a deterministic $T_\varepsilon>0$ such that
$\mathbb P(\sup_{0<t\le T_\varepsilon}|R_n(t)|/t^j>\varepsilon)\to0$.
For a vector or tuple remainder, replace absolute value by its stated norm.
:::

[]{#proof-compression-fl-motion}

::: {.proof}

On the probability-tending-to-one event of @lem-compression-fit, all relevant
operators, feature RMS and residuals have deterministic bounds. The readout
equation gives $\|W^{(L+1)}(t)\|_2/\sqrt n=O(t)$; backpropagation gives
$\|\delta_a^{(\ell)}(t)\|_2/\sqrt n=O(t)$.
For hidden parameter tuples use the norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{par}}$ from
@lem-compression-fit with a zero readout component. Integration of hidden
updates and forward subtraction give, uniformly over the input sphere and
$0\le t\le1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|(W^{(\ell)}(t)-W^{(\ell)}(0))_{\ell=1}^L\|_{\mathrm{par}}&=O(t^2),\\
\frac{\|z^{(\ell)}(t,x)-z^{(\ell)}(0,x)\|_2
 +\|h^{(\ell)}(t,x)-h^{(\ell)}(0,x)\|_2}{\sqrt n}&=O(t^2),\\
f_n(t,x)&=t\dot f_n(0,x)+O(t^2).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-real-bounds}

For the last line, the readout equation gives
$\|\dot W^{(L+1)}(t)-\dot W^{(L+1)}(0)\|_2/\sqrt n=O(t)$;
integrate and use $f_n=(W^{(L+1)})^T h^{(L)}/n$. No new bootstrap is needed.

The remainder control uses an elementary estimate. For bounded Lipschitz
$g$ and an initial vector $u$,

$$
\frac{\|[g(z)-g(z_0)]\odot u\|_2^2}{n}
\le \operatorname{Lip}(g)^2D^2\frac{\|z-z_0\|_2^2}{n}
 +4\|g\|_\infty^2\frac{\|u\mathbf1_{|u|>D}\|_2^2}{n}.
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-multiplier}

Split at $|u_i|=D$. The deterministic row-law limits with second moments
in @lem-compression-fl-initial-fields imply that, for every $\eta>0$, a
fixed cutoff $D$ makes the probability of any needed initial squared tail
exceeding $\eta$ tend to zero. Choose $D$ first, then a small time in
@eq-compression-fl-real-bounds. Gate differences times initial fields are
therefore $o_*(1)$ in Euclidean norm divided by $\sqrt n$, uniformly also
along the segment joining $z_0$ to $z$.

For this proof put $k=2/m$ and define initial vectors by
$P_a^{(L)}=\sum_b y_bh_b^{(L)}(0)$,
$B_a^{(\ell)}=(\phi^{(\ell)})'(z_a^{(\ell)}(0))\odot P_a^{(\ell)}$, and
$P_a^{(\ell-1)}=(W^{(\ell)}(0))^T B_a^{(\ell)}$ for $\ell\ge2$.
The readout divided by $t$ differs from its initial velocity by $O(t)$ in
Euclidean norm divided by $\sqrt n$. Downward subtraction of the backward
recursion and then integration of the hidden updates yield

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\|\delta_a^{(\ell)}(t)-ktB_a^{(\ell)}\|_2}{\sqrt n}&=o_*(t),\\
\left\|\left(W^{(\ell)}(t)-W^{(\ell)}(0)
 -\tfrac12t^2\ddot W^{(\ell)}(0)\right)_{\ell=1}^L
 \right\|_{\mathrm{par}}&=o_*(t^2).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-weight-expansion}

For completeness, each backward difference is the next-layer error through
bounded operators, an $O(t^2)$ operator increment acting on $B$, and a gate
difference acting on $P$, controlled by @eq-compression-fl-multiplier.
Insert this into the updates with $r=-y+O(t)$ and
$\|h(t)-h(0)\|_2/\sqrt n=O(t^2)$, and integrate.
The identities $\|uv^T\|_F/\sqrt n=(\|u\|_2/\sqrt n)\|v\|_2$ and
$\|uh^T\|_F/n=(\|u\|_2/\sqrt n)(\|h\|_2/\sqrt n)$ give the stated
matrix-norm remainder.

Rather than expanding each forward feature, test its increment against $P$.
Locally write $E_{1,n}=\|\ddot W^{(1)}(0)\|_F^2/n$ and
$E_{\ell,n}=\|\ddot W^{(\ell)}(0)\|_F^2$ for $\ell\ge2$.
The integral formula for an activation increment and
@eq-compression-fl-multiplier give

$$
\frac{(P_a^{(\ell)})^T[h_a^{(\ell)}(t)-h_a^{(\ell)}(0)]}{n}
=\frac{(B_a^{(\ell)})^T[z_a^{(\ell)}(t)-z_a^{(\ell)}(0)]}{n}
 +o_*(t^2).
$$

Indeed the error is bounded by the RMS gate difference times $P$, multiplied
by $\|z(t)-z(0)\|_2/\sqrt n=O(t^2)$. Expand the preactivation increment as

$$
\begin{split}
z_a^{(\ell)}(t)-z_a^{(\ell)}(0)
={}&[W^{(\ell)}(t)-W^{(\ell)}(0)]h_a^{(\ell-1)}(0)\\
&+W^{(\ell)}(0)[h_a^{(\ell-1)}(t)-h_a^{(\ell-1)}(0)]\\
&+[W^{(\ell)}(t)-W^{(\ell)}(0)]
 [h_a^{(\ell-1)}(t)-h_a^{(\ell-1)}(0)].
\end{split}
$$

The last term has RMS $O(t^4)$. Sum the first term's pairings with
$y_aB_a^{(\ell)}$ and use @eq-compression-fl-forces and
@eq-compression-fl-weight-expansion: the result is
$t^2E_{\ell,n}/(2k^2)+o_*(t^2)$. The second term pairs the lower feature
increment with $P_a^{(\ell-1)}$. At the first layer only the first term
is present, with the fixed input $v_a$. Telescoping gives

$$
\sum_a y_a\frac{(P_a^{(\ell)})^T
 [h_a^{(\ell)}(t)-h_a^{(\ell)}(0)]}{n}
=\frac{t^2}{2k^2}\sum_{j\le\ell}E_{j,n}+o_*(t^2).
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-adjoint}

All energies have positive limits. Cauchy--Schwarz, using the bounded quantity
$\sum_a y_a^2\|P_a^{(\ell)}\|_2^2/n$, proves the claimed feature-motion
lower bound in every layer on one deterministic small interval.

The tangent kernel on the training set is

$$
\begin{split}
K_{ab}(t)={}&\frac{(h_a^{(L)})^T h_b^{(L)}}n
 +(v_a^T v_b)\frac{(\delta_a^{(1)})^T\delta_b^{(1)}}n\\
&+\sum_{\ell=2}^L
 \frac{(\delta_a^{(\ell)})^T\delta_b^{(\ell)}}n
 \frac{(h_a^{(\ell-1)})^T h_b^{(\ell-1)}}n.
\end{split}
$$

All fields on the right are evaluated at $t$.
@eq-compression-fl-real-bounds gives $K(t)-K(0)=O(t^2)$ in
operator norm. Its readout part, contracted with $y$, is twice the
top pairing in @eq-compression-fl-adjoint, plus $O(t^4)$.
By @eq-compression-fl-weight-expansion and the squared outer products in
@eq-compression-fl-forces, the hidden contribution has the same coefficient.
Consequently

$$
y^T[K(t)-K(0)]y=\frac{2t^2}{k^2}\sum_{\ell=1}^L E_{\ell,n}+o_*(t^2).
$$

The dense flow satisfies $\dot f_n=kK(t)(y-f_n)$; the frozen flow uses $K(0)$.
Their difference is exactly

$$
k\int_0^t e^{-kK(0)(t-s)}[K(s)-K(0)](y-f_n(s))\,ds.
$$

Here $f_n(s)=O(s)$ and the exponential is $I+O(t-s)$ since $K(0)$ is
bounded. Pair with $y$ and integrate the preceding display for the kernel.
The extra terms are $O(t^4)$, giving $2/(3k)=m/3$ in
@eq-compression-fl-cubic.
:::

::: {#lem-compression-fl-nonlinear-increment}
### The nonlinear feature component moves

Let $V=\operatorname{span}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$, with normalized surface measure
$\sigma_V$ on its unit sphere $S(V)$. For sufficiently small fixed $t>0$,
with probability tending to one,

$$
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\inf_{a\in V,\,b\in\mathbb R}
\int_{S(V)}\left|h_i^{(1)}(t,\sqrt d\,v)-h_i^{(1)}(0,\sqrt d\,v)
 -a^T v-b\right|^2\,d\sigma_V(v)\ge c_*t^4.
$$ {#eq-compression-fl-nonlinear-increment}
:::

[]{#proof-compression-fl-nonlinear-increment}

::: {.proof}

Since $\dim V\ge2$, for nonzero $g,r\in V$ the function
$(\phi^{(1)})'(g^T v)(r^T v)$ is not affine on $S(V)$.
Otherwise its values on $r^\perp$ and antipodes force that affine function
to equal $\lambda r^T v$. Off the equator divide by $r^T v$, then use
continuity: $(\phi^{(1)})'$ would be constant on $[-\|g\|_2,\|g\|_2]$,
contradicting analyticity and nonaffineness.

Project the initial first-layer row onto $V$ and call it $g_i$; call its
acceleration row $r_i\in V$. By @lem-compression-fl-initial-fields, their
joint empirical law converges with second moments; $g$ is nondegenerate
Gaussian and $\mathbb E\|r\|_2^2>0$. The squared distance of
$(\phi^{(1)})'(g^T v)(r^T v)$ from affine functions in $L^2(\sigma_V)$ is
continuous in $(g,r)$, bounded by
$\|(\phi^{(1)})'\|_\infty^2\|r\|_2^2$, and positive whenever both are
nonzero. Its empirical mean therefore tends to a positive constant.

The first-layer expansion in @eq-compression-fl-weight-expansion and the
bounded first derivative reduce the actual increment to the fixed row
direction $t^2r_i/2$. On $\|r_i\|_2\le D$, its Taylor remainder divided
by $t^2$ is at most $\|(\phi^{(1)})''\|_\infty t^2D^2/8$; on the complement
it is at most $\|(\phi^{(1)})'\|_\infty\|r_i\|_2$.
The deterministic second-moment limit, choosing $D$ and then time, gives
$o_*(t^2)$ in the $L^2$ space with measure
$n^{-1}\sum_i\delta_i\otimes\sigma_V$ (here $\delta_i$ is a point mass).
Orthogonal projection off affine functions is contractive, so the positive
limiting projected acceleration proves the claim.
:::

[]{#proof-compression-nonlinear-learning}

::: {.proof}

**Proof of @thm-compression-nonlinear-learning.**
The four-point combination in @eq-compression-fl-witnesses, initial velocity
convergence, and @eq-compression-fl-real-bounds give a positive multiple
of $t$ for the dense predictor on a width-independent small interval.
It annihilates every affine predictor and has coefficient absolute sum one,
so it bounds their uniform distance below. The positive energy limit in
@eq-compression-fl-cubic, divided by $\|y\|_1$, similarly gives a training-input
gap of order $t^3$ from the frozen kernel. The two preceding lemmas supply
the internal feature conclusions.

For each fixed positive time, the vanishing absolute errors of
@prp-compression-legendre, @prp-compression-harmonic, and
@prp-compression-panel transfer both prediction gaps by the triangle
inequality. Eventual bounds at every confidence imply convergence in
probability; the relative-variability statement alone is not needed for
this step. Choose common smaller $c_*,t_*>0$.
Legendre and Harmonic already cover the witnesses. Taylor appends them
before initialization, without labels or additional training terms.
Replacing $p$ by at most $p+4$ multiplies the quadratic panel factor by at
most $9$ and the linear data factor by at most $3$, since $m+p\ge2$.
No endpoint gap or identification of compressed coordinates with dense
neurons is used or asserted.
:::

## Assembly of the headline theorem {#sec-compression-assembly}

[]{#proof-compression-headline}

::::::::::::::: {.proof}

**Proof of @thm-compression-headline.**

The preceding constructions provide the stated retained counts and the
initialized-jet provenance alternative; the efficient alternatives have
their own execution proofs. Here we verify the original asymptotic
comparison. @thm-compression-polynomial-width gives its separate quantitative
strengthening for Legendre and Taylor. The reference is actual dense
variability. The following proof does not compare against a dense upper certificate.
Fix a confidence budget $0<\delta_0<1$. By @prp-compression-dense-lower, for
sufficiently large width,

$$
\Pr\left\{\left\lVert f_n-\widetilde f_n\right\rVert_{\mathcal X}
 \ge c_{\phi,L,\delta_0}
       \frac{Y\sqrt\gamma}{\sqrt n[\log(en)]^{5/2}}\right\}
 \ge1-\delta_0.
$$

Its witness is a training input, so the same lower bound applies on either
promised domain. The source and fitting events give all required limits.
The Legendre order of @prp-compression-legendre gives error at most
$CY/(\sqrt n[\log(en)]^3)$; its ratio to the displayed lower bound is
at most a fixed-problem, fixed-confidence multiple of
$[\log(en)]^{-1/2}$. For the two selected models,
@prp-compression-harmonic and @prp-compression-panel give error at most $Y/n$, and the corresponding
ratio is at most

$$
\frac{[\log(en)]^{5/2}}
 {c_{\phi,L,\delta_0}\sqrt{\gamma n}}\longrightarrow0.
$$

Intersecting each approximation event with the lower event costs at most
$2\delta_0$ by the union bound, without any independence requirement.
For every fixed positive ratio tolerance the limiting superior of its failure
probability is therefore at most $2\delta_0$. Letting $\delta_0\downarrow0$
proves @eq-compression-relative, including the stated failure convention.
For @eq-compression-absolute, use the selected-model event at the requested
confidence. The label assumption stays fixed throughout; no label inequality
is used to reduce a displayed sample/gap power.
